title: Scaling Normalizer & Surge-Credit Adaptor for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Ravi Mehta
description:
Summary:
This ticket captures design and implementation work for a new Autoscaling Policy Engine component that sits between the telemetry layer and the low-level scaler. The component (Scaling Normalizer & Surge-Credit Adaptor) has three responsibilities: 1) normalize heterogeneous tenant SLAs and raw signals into a unified Headroom Index; 2) run a hybrid scaling algorithm (PID + bounded-model-predictive) that respects derivative and step-rate safety limits; 3) manage a bounded surge-credit system with decay and reconciliation to allow controlled short bursts without destabilizing fleet-level guarantees.

Motivation and context:
- Current autoscalers operate on raw metrics (p95 latency, tokens/sec, queue depth) and apply separate heuristics per fleet, which makes multi-tenant guarantees inconsistent and leads to oscillations during flash traffic.
- We need a single intermediary that can express policies in terms of normalized targets (Headroom Index) and apply safety limits consistently across Dedicated fleets so capacity commits remain predictable.

Design overview (high level):
1) Target normalization layer: maps metric vector -> Headroom Index (HI) in [0, 1.5]. Inputs: p50/p95 latency (ms), tokens/sec per GPU, queue depth, KV cache hit ratio, cold-warm ratio. Normalization rules are configurable per customer class (enterprise, standard). Example score: HI = clamp(1 + alpha*(p95/p95_target - 1) + beta*(desired_tps/current_tps - 1) - gamma*cache_hit, 0, 1.5).
2) Hybrid scaling algorithm: primary controller is a PID tuned on HI with a derivative clamp to avoid spiky responses. Secondary predictive layer uses a lightweight model-predictive step when a sustained delta in HI persists for multiple windows (3 windows default). The algorithm outputs a suggested capacity delta (GPU_count delta), then the safety arbiter applies fences.
3) Safety arbiter and surge-credit adaptor: enforces: max_step_up, max_step_down, max_derivative (GPU change per minute), and a surge-credit bucket per tenant/fleet. Credits are earned by underutilization at a configured rate and consumed during bursts. Credits decay exponentially (half-life parameter) so old credits don't accumulate indefinitely. A reconciliation process drains credits if SLA drift exceeds threshold.

Concrete rules & parameters (initial):
- control_window: 30s sampling
- HI target: 1.0 (normalized steady-state)
- pid: P=1.1, I=0.25, D=0.15 (tunable per SKU)
- derivative_clamp: +/- 2 GPUs per 60s per pool
- max_step_up: 5 GPUs, max_step_down: 10 GPUs (global limits)
- surge_credit_max: defined as percentage of fleet commit (default 25%)
- credit_earn_rate: 0.02 * committed_capacity_per_minute
- credit_decay_half_life: 6 hours
- predictive_window_threshold: 3 windows before MPC engages

Telemetry and signals required:
- per-tenant: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, in-queue depth, KV cache hit%, model seq length distribution
- per-fleet: total_allocated_gpus, active_jobs, cold_warm_ratio, average_kv_evict_rate
- derived: Headroom Index, credit_balance, recent_gpu_delta_history

Acceptance criteria (deploy gating):
- unit/e2e tests for HI mapping, PID behavior, derivative clamp enforcement and credit accounting
- can run in simulation (historical replay) against 30-day trace with at least 95% fewer oscillations vs baseline and no regressions to committed throughput SLAs
- dashboards: HI per-tenant, credit balance, safety-arbiter actions (blocked step-ups), and rollout telemetry available in Console
- rollout plan with canary: 5% of Dedicated traffic in Canary for 72h, rollback if p95 above SLA by >20% for >15m

Implementation plan (initial phases):
- Phase A (design + infra hooks): 1 week - finalize HI formula and param registry; expose signals from telemetry; define wire contract with scaler orchestrator.
- Phase B (sim & CI): 2 weeks - build simulator that replays historical traces and runs candidate controllers; automatic comparator with baseline autoscaler.
- Phase C (canary + metrics): 2 weeks - deploy to 5% fleet, observe, tune PID and credit params, document incident playbook.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Granularity of credits: per-tenant vs per-fleet. Proposal: per-tenant with tiered caps to avoid noisy tenants exhausting pool credits.
- Credit decay math: exponential decay preferred to prevent banked credits forever, but parameterization needs customer-specific guardrails.
- Interaction with spot/burst capacity: should credit consumption trigger spot instance acquisition? Proposal: allow only if cost budget permits and only for P0 tenants.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: mis-tuned HI mapping can permanently bias scaling. Mitigation: gated canary with synthetic load tests and automatic rollback on drift.
- Risk: credits permit long bursts that violate provider commit. Mitigation: global credit floor and alerts when fleet-level credit consumption > X%.

Docs & artifacts linked:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.internal/confluence/dedicated-autoscale/normalizer-design (placeholder)
- Simulator repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscale-sim/pull/187 (placeholder)
